Tell the page what is in front of you, and it tells you how to read it. The lessons behind it start at
[Alto and Tenor Clefs](/lessons/score-clefs.qmd).

## Your part

<div class="pr-form">
<div><label for="pr-inst">Instrument named on the part</label><select id="pr-inst"></select></div>
<div><label for="pr-var">In (its key)</label><select id="pr-var"></select></div>
<div><label for="pr-from">The key signature I have is</label><select id="pr-from">
<option value="part">on the part (written)</option><option value="concert">in a concert-pitch score (sounding)</option></select></div>
<div><label for="pr-key">Key signature</label><select id="pr-key"></select></div>
<div><label for="pr-play">I will play it on</label><select id="pr-play"></select></div>
</div>

## How to read it

<div class="pr-out" id="pr-out"></div>

## Written and sounding

<div class="pr-staves">
<figure><figcaption id="pr-cap-w">As written on the part</figcaption><div id="pr-w"></div></figure>
<figure><figcaption id="pr-cap-s">As it sounds (concert pitch)</figcaption><div id="pr-s"></div><button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="pr-hear">▶ Hear it</button></figure>
</div>

The sounding staff is at its real octave, so a big transposition (tuba, double bass, glockenspiel) shows
ledger lines that the written part was made to avoid. That is the point of the octave transposition.

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var S = ScoreReading, $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var inst = $("pr-inst"), vr = $("pr-var"), from = $("pr-from"), key = $("pr-key"), play = $("pr-play");
  var fam = {}; S.INSTRUMENTS.forEach(function (i) { (fam[i.family] = fam[i.family] || []).push(i); });
  function fill(sel, withConcert) {
    if (withConcert) sel.add(new Option("a concert-pitch instrument (piano, voice…)", ""));
    Object.keys(fam).forEach(function (f) {
      var g = document.createElement("optgroup"); g.label = f;
      fam[f].forEach(function (i) { i.variants.forEach(function (v, k) {
        if (withConcert || k === 0) g.appendChild(new Option(withConcert ? i.name + (i.variants.length > 1 || v.key !== "C" ? " in " + v.key : "") : i.name, withConcert ? i.id + ":" + k : i.id));
      }); });
      sel.appendChild(g);
    });
  }
  fill(inst, false); fill(play, true);
  for (var f = -7; f <= 7; f++) key.add(new Option(S.sigName(f) + " (" + S.keyName(f) + " / " + S.keyName(f, true) + ")", f));
  key.value = 0;
  try { var saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("part-reader") || "null"); } catch (e) {}
  function variants() {
    var i = S.find(inst.value); vr.innerHTML = "";
    i.variants.forEach(function (v, k) { vr.add(new Option(v.key, k)); });
  }
  inst.value = (saved && saved.inst) || "clar"; variants();
  if (saved) { vr.value = saved.v || 0; from.value = saved.from || "part"; key.value = saved.key || 0; play.value = saved.play || ""; }
  [inst, vr, from, key, play].forEach(function (e) { e.addEventListener("change", function () { if (e === inst) variants(); go(); }); });

  var lastSound = null, hearH = null;
  function draw(id, abc) { return ABCJS.renderAbc(id, abc, { responsive: "resize", add_classes: true, paddingtop: 0, paddingbottom: 0 })[0]; }

  function go() {
    var i = S.find(inst.value), v = i.variants[+vr.value], semis = v.semis, k = +key.value;
    try { localStorage.setItem("part-reader", JSON.stringify({ inst: inst.value, v: vr.value, from: from.value, key: key.value, play: play.value })); } catch (e) {}
    var written = from.value === "part" ? k : S.moveKey(k, -semis);
    var concert = S.moveKey(written, semis);
    var who = i.name + (v.key !== "C" || i.variants.length > 1 ? " in " + v.key : "");
    var h = "";
    h += "<div class='pr-big'>" + (from.value === "part"
      ? "Part in " + S.keyName(written) + " → sounds in " + S.keyName(concert)
      : "Concert " + S.keyName(concert) + " → the " + who + " part is in " + S.keyName(written)) + "</div>";
    h += "<p>(Minor keys: " + S.keyName(written, true) + " on the part = " + S.keyName(concert, true) + " concert.) ";
    h += "Every note of the " + who + " part sounds <b>" + S.intervalName(semis) + "</b> than written" + (semis ? "" : "") + ".</p>";
    h += "<h3>Steps</h3><ol>";
    if (from.value === "concert") h += "<li>The part shows " + S.sigName(written) + ". To get there from the score, move the key and every note " + S.intervalName(-semis).replace(/ lower$/, " down").replace(/ higher$/, " up") + ".</li>";
    // the instrument actually played
    var p = play.value ? play.value.split(":") : null, pi = p ? S.find(p[0]) : null, pv = pi ? pi.variants[+p[1]] : { key: "C", semis: 0, clefs: v.clefs };
    var playName = pi ? pi.name + " in " + pv.key : "a concert-pitch instrument";
    var shift = semis - pv.semis, pk = S.moveKey(written, shift);
    if (!pi || pi.id !== i.id || pv !== v) {
      h += "<li>You are playing it on " + playName + ". Read each written note " + (shift ? S.intervalName(shift).replace(/ lower$/, " lower").replace(/ higher$/, " higher") : "as written") +
        (shift ? ", and think in the key of <b>" + S.keyName(pk) + "</b> (" + S.sigName(pk) + ")" : "") + ".";
      if (Math.abs(shift) >= 12 && pi) h += " Most of that is octave: drop the octave part and play where the instrument sits comfortably.";
      if (!pi && Math.abs(semis) >= 12) h += " If your instrument can't reach that octave, play it an octave nearer and say so.";
      h += "</li>";
    } else h += "<li>Your instrument matches the part: read it as written, in " + S.sigName(written) + ".</li>";
    h += "<li>Clefs you may meet on this part:<ul>" + v.clefs.map(function (c) { return "<li>" + S.CLEF_TIPS[c] + "</li>"; }).join("") + "</ul></li>";
    if (/basso|alto/.test(v.key)) h += "<li><i>Basso</i> and <i>alto</i> tell you which octave: B♭ basso sounds a 9th below the written note, B♭ alto only a 2nd below.</li>";
    if (i.id === "horn" && semis !== -7) h += "<li>Horn players read this on the F horn by moving every note " + S.intervalName(semis + 7).replace(/^a /, "") + ". Older horn parts often have no key signature: the accidentals are written in front of each note.</li>";
    if (i.id === "tpt" && v.key !== "B♭" && v.key !== "C") h += "<li>Older trumpet parts were also often written without a key signature. Check the accidentals.</li>";
    h += "</ol>";
    if (v.note) h += "<p class='pr-note'>" + v.note + "</p>";
    $("pr-out").innerHTML = h;

    var ws = S.writtenAndSounding(written, semis, v.clefs[0]);
    draw("pr-w", ws.written); lastSound = draw("pr-s", ws.sounding);
    $("pr-cap-w").textContent = "As written on the " + who + " part";
  }
  $("pr-hear").addEventListener("click", function () {
    if (hearH) { hearH.stop(); hearH = null; this.textContent = "▶ Hear it"; return; }
    var b = this; b.textContent = "■ Stop";
    hearH = AbcPlay.play(lastSound, { sound: "piano", qpm: 100, onEnd: function () { hearH = null; b.textContent = "▶ Hear it"; } });
  });
  go();
})();
</script>
<script src="/apps/shared/lessons/sections.js?v=1"></script>
```

## Works Cited

::: {.works-cited}
**For students**

"Transposing Instrument." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposing_instrument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposing_instrument). Concert-pitch scores (Prokofiev), horn bass clef ambiguity, crooks, brass-band trombone in B♭.

**For teachers**

Adler, Samuel. *The Study of Orchestration*. 4th ed., W. W. Norton, 2016. Instrument ranges, clefs and transpositions.

Gould, Elaine. *Behind Bars: The Definitive Guide to Music Notation*. Faber Music, 2011. Grace notes, trills and other ornaments in modern notation.
:::
